A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cross-sections for the reaction pp → π o x are well described by a simple power law in p ⊥, with a power which is approximately constant over the whole range of p ⊥, √ s and centre-of-mass angle studied.
the invariant cross-section of π o production in p-p collisions can be described with a power-law dependence on p ⊥ and s, with n ≈ 8.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the invariant cross-section of the reaction p + p→πo+anything is well described by a simple power-law dependence on p ⊥, which is consistent with perturbative QCD calculations.
the pion cross sections at high p ⊥ and high energy are well described by a simple scaling law, with a power-law dependence on p ⊥ and √ s, and a weak dependence of the power law on s.
the pion production cross-section increases as a function of energy, but at a slower rate than that of the total cross-section.
